newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close short day mostly lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close short day mostly lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed an abbreviated trading session mostly lower after light pre-holiday activity.
Chicago currency futures shut early Tuesday at 1200 CST/1800 GMT, will stay closed Wednesday and will resume normal pit trading hours Thursday.
The Swiss franc and yen stayed under the most pressure, with March Swiss eroding the most on crosses, technicals and fundamentals that suggest Swiss interest rates will remain low.
March Swiss franc futures fell to a new contract low at $0.7476 during pit trading hours.
The Swiss National Bank aggressively added liquidity Tuesday, and an SNB spokesman saying the central bank "wanted to avoid rates moving upwards."
Traders said the easy-money stance of the Swiss central bank appeared unchanged, and one broker attributed the further decline in the Swiss currency to year-end adjustments.
"It seems like a lot of liquidation in the Swiss because the open interest keeps declining," one floor broker said of the steady erosion in March futures.
March yen came within ticks of its $0.008835 contract low, with brokers looking for that level to give way soon.
March yen lacked power to punch much below support at the $0.008840 area, which corresponds to about 114.50 spot.
Yen suffered partly from the overnight slide in Japan's Nikkei 225 stock index, which fell some 529 points to a one-year low of 19,161.71 at Tokyo's close.
Sterling gave up some of Monday's gains and backed off from its overnight peak hit after news that Britain's global trade deficit shrank in October, paced by a jump in exports.
But traders said the unit remained buoyed by ideas U.K. rates could rise again soon after recent comments by Bank of England Governor Eddie George.
Futures turnover Tuesday stayed very light, estimated on the price boards at about 5,000, 3,400 and 3,300 contracts in March Swiss francs, marks and yen, respectively, brokers added.

At settlement, March yen fell $0.000030 to $0.008841, marks eased $0.0010 to $0.6454, Swiss francs dropped $0.0050 to $0.7484, sterling declined $0.0024 to $1.6706, Canadian dollar firmed $0.0008 to $0.7367, Aussie dollar eased $0.0013 to $0.7967, and Mexican peso firmed $0.000050 to $0.121750.
